text:
maria: quick note — after we flipped the kernel-chooser heuristic last night, canary shows a host-side parse CPU increase for streaming tiny messages. noticed during synthetic replay.
lee: thanks, spotted it in the ingress tail charts. single-token p99 jumped ~85ms at first.
ajay: i profiled a canary instance. root cause looks like a change in frame representation (framerepr v2) that forces a memcpy when a stream fragment spans buffer boundaries. stack: runtime::stream_parse -> framerepr::to_proto -> memcpy.
kevin: is this a kernel-side invariant we missed? we changed how fragments are chained.
ajay: yeah, kernel assumes contiguous buffer view which host code previously gave; new chooser gives a non-contig span so host code copies to coalesce. that memcpy is hitting hot path on small messages.
maria: mitigation options?
lee: 1) quick rollback of kernel-chooser (fast, low-risk). 2) host-side zero-copy view that understands framerepr v2 (medium). 3) keep kernel but add a fast-path in ingress for small-fragment inline coalesce (medium-fast).
ajay: i'm prototyping `decode_view` — zero-copy proto view over incoming iovecs, avoids memcpy by pointing into buffer slices and only copies if message crosses two iovecs and we can't reference both. also adding small heuristic: if message_len < 256 bytes, prefer in-place parse.
maria: also saw batching shrink — avg batch tokens dropped which increased per-token overhead. any relationship?
ajay: yes — because inter-arrival timing changed slightly (16us -> 90us median), our batcher fired earlier. current policy is size-first; new kernel increases jitter so we should bias towards time-window when inter-arrival > 50us for stream workloads.
kevin: could be two regressions: memcpy CPU and smaller batches. fix both in a host patch and run canary. ops prefers rollback to stop noise, but we need a verified patch quickly.
lee: rolling back kernel-chooser now. runtime-bot: deploy started service=ingress-canary tag=chooser-rollback-175999 (commit=f4d2b0) ETA 90s. :white_check_mark:
ajay: local microbench (k8s synthetic traces):
```
baseline (pre-change): host_parse_p50=1.1ms p95=2.9ms kvcache_hit=0.81 avg_batch_tokens=30
after-change (kernel-chooser): host_parse_p50=2.0ms p95=4.5ms kvcache_hit=0.78 avg_batch_tokens=14
host-patch (decode_view + time-pref batch): host_parse_p50=1.0ms p95=1.6ms kvcache_hit=0.82 avg_batch_tokens=29
```
maria: nice. the kvcache hit slightly improved with decode_view — maybe fewer allocations and less churn. can you include flame graphs?
ajay: will attach perf flame and the bench harness. putting branch `perf/zero-copy-decode-175999` up shortly.
kevin: tests to run after we land: 24h mixed-latency replay, KV eviction graph, p99 decode CPU, socket smallwrite burst patterns. add an ablation where batcher keeps size-first to show regression.
lee: also add a unit test for framerepr v2 that simulates fragmented iovecs to avoid future regressions.
maria: thanks. once patch lands, coordinate with infra to run canary under production-ish traffic. don't forget to update the perf alert thresholds if deploy changes baseline.
runtime-bot: rollback complete for service=ingress-canary tag=chooser-rollback-175999 (status=success)
kevin: small follow-up: consider adding a kernel hint in chooser that prefers contiguous framing for low-latency flight — that would avoid surprises when host lacks zero-copy. file an RFC?
maria: please open RFC in `#eng-runtime` and reference this thread. good catch everyone.
